messages:
Arjun: Quick sync - I'm prototyping a per-request "precision-affinity" hint that clients can set (metadata header / rpc proto). Not a hard override, more a preference that the admission layer tries to honor. Thinking uses: latency-sensitive UI flows want fp8 lanes, high-fidelity generation wants int8/32.
Priya: Love having a small surface for this. Two immediate concerns: batching semantics and kv-cache compatibility. If we mix affinities in a batch, what happens?
Gabe: Rule idea: admission groups by effective affinity for batching. Mixed-affinity requests are either 1) split into separate batches, or 2) served on the highest-quality lane that can handle all. Splitting increases scheduling pressure.
Riley: Also KV cache: if a request pins a 4bit lane but the cached KV was generated in int8, we need a consistent rule. Either: invalidate cache for that session, or allow cross-precision reuse with serialization normalization.
Arjun: Proposal: affinity has two flags: "degree" (prefer|require) and "cache_compat" (allow|no-allow). Default = prefer + allow. If require + no-allow and not supported -> admission rejects with structured error.
Priya: Nice. How do we surface stored profile mapping? We shouldn't let every request create new runtime lanes. Suggest a quant affinity registry that maps common affinities to canonical lane IDs. Registry entries have quality score and cost multiplier. Admission resolves affinity -> lane_id.
Gabe: That registry should also include a "warmup_samples" field. For a new lane we take 1k shadowed requests to compute perf and small evals to sanity-check quality before enabling batching optimizations.
Riley: Ops note: we need billing labels for each lane (for per-token accounting). Add labels: lane_id, affinity_hint, profile_version. Keep it small.
Arjun: Telemetry events: precision_affinity.requested, resolved_lane_id, cache_action (used|invalidated|converted), fallback_path, quality_delta_estimate, latency_p99_delta. Keep payload <1KB.
Priya: Rollback triggers: if quality_delta_estimate > 0.02 (user-facing) or error_rate jumps > 50% relative. For subtle quality issues, require offline eval to declare regen.
Gabe: Testing: run a shadow replay for a week using production traces, compute per-lane regressions vs baseline. If regressions under thresholds, enable canary at 0.5% then 5% then 25%.
Riley: Implementation detail: admission cache TTL 60s, owner API to invalidate per-customer. When lane profile mutates, increment profile_version and surface in-flight version header so we don't mutate in-flight behavior.
Arjun: One more: interactions with batching heuristics. If a lane has stricter max_seq_len or different kernel, we tag kernels with lane_id and let scheduler prefer co-locating matching lane batches. Nonmatching samples may pay a penalty but should still succeed.
OpsBot: Canary rollout scheduled: precision-affinity-registry v0.1 -> canary, traffic=0.5%.
Arjun: I'll write a short RFC with the registry schema, admission algorithm, and a test checklist. Priya/Gabe/Riley please add notes to the RFC PR.
